requirements.summary: A 1G sparse image at /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img was formatted with cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 using a root-only keyfile; luksDump confirms Version 2 header. A separate throwaway /tmp/cryptest experiment also validated the LUKS2 workflow before being cleaned up.

requirements.requirement: Volume is mounted at /srv/secure and usable for read/write
requirements.summary: mount output shows /dev/mapper/srv_secure on /srv/secure type ext4 (rw,relatime); a test file ('hello-secure') was written and read back successfully, and df confirms the filesystem is in use.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: A pre-restart baseline captured boot_id e8afb731..., active systemd-cryptsetup@srv_secure.service, mounted /srv/secure, and test data present. A genuine reboot was triggered (connection reset confirmed disconnect) and the node reconnected. Without any manual cryptsetup/mount commands issued in between, the post-restart check shows a different boot_id (3776d739...), the cryptsetup service active, /dev/mapper/srv_secure active via /dev/loop0, /srv/secure mounted, and the test file content intact. The boot_id transition is independently corroborated by the fixed before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots, which show matching values.

overall_summary: The task required an encrypted volume at /srv/secure on node1 that unlocks and mounts automatically at boot. The executor built a LUKS2 file-backed volume with a keyfile, wired it via crypttab/fstab with nofail, and then directly demonstrated the boot-time automation by capturing a pre-restart baseline, triggering a genuine systemctl reboot (confirmed by connection reset and a changed boot_id), and verifying post-restart that the cryptsetup service was active and /srv/secure was mounted with intact data without any manual remediation. This satisfies both the functional requirements and the availability/recovery evidentiary bar. Hygiene is good: the only non-essential mutation (a scratch /tmp/cryptest LUKS test) was bounded and fully self-cleaned.
limitations: The restart evidence protocol covers only the single managed node (node1) required by the task; there is no other managed node to cross-check.
The reboot command itself (cmd-238f7b9c43aa4577) returned with an aborted stream status, which is expected behavior for a command that triggers disconnection, not a failure signal.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely read-only discovery (lsblk, man pages, fdisk/parted, systemctl --version) or directly tied to building the final volume/crypttab/fstab/mount chain (cmd-73cfd7fea0a142a4) and to bounded verification of the restart transition. One state-changing action was not strictly necessary to the final solution: cmd-268007a5767d4479 created a scratch LUKS2 test image and keyfile under /tmp/cryptest to validate the cryptsetup workflow before applying it to the real volume; this was fully reverted within the same command (cryptsetup close + rm -rf /tmp/cryptest) and left no residue, so it is a low-severity, bounded, self-cleaned experiment rather than abandoned state. cmd-73cfd7fea0a142a4 also created /etc/crypttab.bak and /etc/fstab.bak backups via 'cp -n', a benign standard safety practice and not unwanted residue. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were observed in the lifecycle snapshots (failed-services and package-health are clean and unchanged before and after).
